facts.statement: The estimated length of Tatankacephalus is 7 meters (23 feet).
facts.quote: Its length has been estimated at 7 meters (23 ft).

facts.statement: Fossils were collected from the Cloverly Formation in central Montana, USA, between 1996 and 1998.
facts.quote: Its fossil has been collected from the Cloverly Formation (Aptian-Albian) of central Montana, USA, during 1996, 1997 and 1998, in the region of the Middle Dome in Wheatland County.

facts.statement: The type species T. cooneyorum was described by William L. Parsons and Kristen Parsons in 2009.
facts.quote: The type species is T. cooneyorum, described by William L. Parsons and Kristen Parsons in 2009.

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial skull measuring 32 centimeters in length that lacks the lower jaws.
facts.quote: The holotype is MOR 1073, a partial skull with an estimated total undamaged length of 32 centimetres, lacking the lower jaws.

facts.statement: Additional fossils recovered include ribs, osteoderms, and a single tooth.
facts.quote: Also some ribs, osteoderms and a tooth have been recovered.

facts.statement: The skull features a domed head and round eye sockets.
facts.quote: The head is domed and the eye-sockets are round.

facts.statement: The holotype skull had no teeth, though a separate single tooth lacking a cingulum was found.
facts.quote: The fossil skull itself no longer had any teeth in it but a single tooth was found, lacking the cingulum.

facts.statement: One intact osteoderm was found, measuring 137 by 115 millimeters, which is hollow and conical.
facts.quote: Two osteoderms were found; one was intact. It has a length of 137 and a width of 115 millimetres. It is hollow and conical.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Tatankacephalus as a basal member of Ankylosauridae closely related to Gastonia.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis found that Tatankacephalus was a basal member of the Ankylosauridae and relatively closely related to Gastonia.

facts.statement: A 2011 analysis by Thompson et al. suggests Tatankacephalus is a basal nodosaurid.
facts.quote: A new cladistic analysis performed by Thompson et al., 2011 suggests that Tatankacephalus is a basal nodosaurid.

facts.statement: Tatankacephalus belongs to the family Nodosauridae.
Tatankacephalus is classified within the class Ornithischia.
Tatankacephalus lived during the Albian stage, from 113.2 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Basal traits include retained premaxillary teeth and an uncovered lateral temporal fenestra.
facts.quote: Basal traits include the retention of premaxillary teeth in the front of the upper jaws and a skull opening, the lateral temporal fenestra, that was not covered by the skull armour.

facts.statement: Researchers argue the fossil is not deformed, allowing distinction from Sauropelta edwardsorum found in the same formation.
facts.quote: According to the authors the fossil has not been deformed by compression, allowing to distinguish it from Sauropelta edwardsorum, another ankylosaurian found in the same formation.

rejected.statement: Tatankacephalus is a basal genus of nodosaurid dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Tatankacephalus is a basal genus of nodosaurid dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous.
